rows.title: The civil birth extract for Ivan Defranceski, 1951
rows.holder: Municipality of Senj — recovered from the MyHeritage media library
rows.what: One document in this archive is a state record rather than a church one or a tree one: the Yugoslav register-of-births extract for Ivan Defranceski, born at Senj Hospital on 17 December 1951 — Senj registration 152/1954, issued 27 April 1954 over the seal of the Municipality of Senj.
rows.carries: It confirms Hedviga's own birth date and place from outside the family tree, and it carries three things the tree does not.

rows.title: Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994
rows.holder: Hrvatski državni arhiv, Zagreb — digitised by FamilySearch
rows.kind: Roman Catholic parish registers (Rimokatolička crkva), Latin and later Croatian, kept by the parish priest
rows.what: Citations in this tree reach specific images in specific volumes. A single baptismal entry typically gives the child, the date, the parents, the house number and the godparents — which is how this archive knows that Milka Papić's godparents were Josip Glavičić and Ivka Filipović, and that Antonija Prpić's were Lucas and Anna Tomljanović.
rows.caution: A caution on the catalogue. One christening citation in this tree — for Nicolaus Žubrinić, Otočac, 1834 — is labelled by FamilySearch as “Osekovo, Belovár-Körös Megye, Hungary records”. The image group and page are right; the catalogue heading is wrong. Anyone re-searching by place name will not find it.

rows.title: The spine: one MyHeritage tree
rows.holder: MyHeritage — exported as GEDCOM on 8 September 2026
rows.what: It is the structure of this archive and the origin of nearly every date. Within it, individual people cite other trees — Geni World Family Tree, Defranceski Family Site, Boras Web Site, Grlica Web Site, Janicic, Marko Karic rodoslov.
rows.caution:
One export, six archives. This is not a Blažević export — it is the whole tree, covering the Defranceski, Lerena, Taylor, Barry, Blažević and Booyzen families, and the sibling archives are built from the same file. So a fact contradicted here is contradicted in all of them, and a re-export refreshes all of them at once. Checked 10 September 2026: still current, and nothing here depends on a newer one.

Many notes carry a SmartCopy stamp from Geni, dated 2014–2017. That records when a record was copied between websites, not when anything was verified. The build strips this boilerplate from the displayed notes and keeps the human prose.

rows.title: An automated surname-origin website
rows.holder: Not named here, because naming it would send readers to it
rows.what: Consulted for Žubrinić and not relied on anywhere here. It offers two unrelated etymologies in the same article, places the name in Dalmatia when its Croatian density is highest in Lika-Senj, and names a “Petar Žubrinić, 18th-century Croatian ban” who did not exist — the bans of that century were Pálffy, Drašković, Eszterházy, Branyng, Batthyány, Nádasdy, Esterházy, Balassa and Erdődy.

rows.title: Never consulted, and it shows
rows.holder: Croatian and South African civil registration; Zimbabwean immigration; Mirogoj cemetery; the Yugoslav war victims register
rows.kind: The records this archive has not obtained
rows.what: No death certificate has been obtained for Hedviga (Johannesburg 2001) or Ivan (Senj 1995), and no extract for the 1920 Senj marriage. No South African or Rhodesian immigration file. No Yugoslav war victims register search for Oto. No Mirogoj cemetery record for Antonija Prpić. These are the next things to do.
